title: Local runtime devkit — lightweight inference dev CLI (brainstorm)
content:
Top-level idea
--------------
We build a tiny developer-facing runtime / CLI that simulates Redwood inference locally for fast iteration: local-devkit.

Why?
- Fast loop for prompt engineering + integration tests without remote quotas or waiting for hosted deploys.
- Better DX on Private onboarding: customers can smoke-test integration before they provision infra.
- Lower friction for building reference apps and examples.

Core principles
- Opinionated and minimal: works out of the box for common use cases (chat, generate, embeddings).
- Reproducible: same basic config keys as Redwood API (model name, max_tokens, temperature).
- Safe defaults: telemetry opt-in, no cloud credentials by default.
- Pluggable: can proxy to a real Redwood endpoint or run a lightweight local runtime (mocked or tiny ggml-style runtime)

Primary personas
- Individual frontend/mobile engineers who need a local mock for integration tests.
- ML engineers iterating on prompts and system messages.
- Solutions engineers running PoCs in customer offices (no internet).

User stories (rough)
- As a frontend dev, I want to run local-devkit start and get a local HTTP endpoint that mirrors Redwood's /v1/chat and /v1/generate so I can call it from my app.
- As an ML engineer, I want to run local-devkit --model redwood-open-7b --quantize quick to run cheap on my laptop for prompt experiments.
- As a solutions engineer, I want an "airgap mode" that uses a packaged runtime image and no external network.

MVP feature surface
- CLI: local-devkit init, start, stop, status, logs
- Local HTTP server: /v1/chat, /v1/generate, /v1/embeddings (subset) with compatible request/response shapes
- Two backends: 1) Mock deterministic backend (fast, no model), 2) Lightweight runtime wrapper (optional, depends on user host capabilities)
- Config: ~/.redwood/local-devkit.yaml with model presets, port, telemetry=false, backend=mock|runtime|proxy
- Proxy mode: forward to Redwood hosted using API_KEY env var (useful for hybrid debugging)
- Quickstart UX: one-command demo that seeds example prompt templates and a tiny example app snippet

CLI UX notes
- Setup flow: local-devkit init (creates config + examples)
- Start: local-devkit start [-p PORT] [--profile small|dev|prod]
- Run a one-off: local-devkit run --file examples/quickchat.json -> prints response (good for CI)
- Integration test mode: local-devkit start --ci -> runs in deterministic seed mode and exits with status codes for assertions

Integration with Redwood products
- Hosted API parity: keep request/response keys aligned to minimize friction switching from local to hosted
- Private deployments: local-devkit can validate ecosystem config (routes, TLS cert format, key rotation steps) by parsing user-provided manifests
- Dedicated: allow smoke tests that validate consumed tokens and latency hooks (simulate latency ranges)

Security / privacy
- Default to telemetry=false; if enabled, only send anonymized event counters (no prompts). Explicit opt-in.
- No keys written to disk unless user runs `local-devkit configure-proxy` which stores token encrypted in OS keystore (macOS keychain, Windows cred manager).
- Airgap mode: provide a single tarball with runtime image + example data; document verification checksums.

Acceptance criteria (MVP)
- devkit can be installed via pip/npm/homebrew (pick 1 for MVP).
- local HTTP endpoint accepts a minimal Chat completion request and returns a deterministic mocked response within 50ms.
- Proxy mode correctly forwards a request to Redwood hosted and returns the same shape of response.
- Developer quickstart: <5 minute time to first response on a laptop with no cloud config.

Open questions / risks
- Do we ship a real local runtime kernel (GGML) or rely on a remote proxy + mock? Shipping a real runtime increases maintenance and binary size.
- Licensing of bundled models: can we include tiny LLM weights in an airgap tarball? Probably not unless OSS-compatible.
- CI integration: do we provide a docker image for test runners? Likely yes.
- Which package manager (pip vs brew vs npm) gives best DX for our primary persona? Survey engineering.

Technical sketch
- Language: Go or Rust for single-binary distribution (fast startup, small deps). Python wrapper for dev UX (if we want fast iteration).
- Server: tiny HTTP layer that maps Redwood API to backend impl.
- Mock backend: rule-based templating (supports system + user messages, simple string interpolation, seeded RNG for reproducibility).
- Runtime backend: thin shim around local model runner (optional plugin interface)

Telemetry & metrics for us (opt-in)
- Events: install, start, backend used, proxy-mode usage counts. No prompt payloads.
- Use to inform which features to prioritize (proxy vs runtime adoption).

Example quickstart (note to self):
1) curl -fsSL https://get.redwood.dev/local-devkit | sh
2) local-devkit init
3) local-devkit start --backend mock
4) curl localhost:8080/v1/chat -H "Authorization: Bearer test" -d '{"messages":[{"role":"user","content":"hello"}],"model":"redwood-mock"}'

TODO (short list)
- [ ] Validate exact Redwood API shapes to emulate (ask API team). (linked: JIRA-RI-4021)
- [ ] Run short survey with 10 frontend/mobile devs to pick packaging strategy (brew vs pip).
- [ ] Prototype mock backend in a small Go binary.
- [ ] Draft internal support doc for Private onboarding team: how to use devkit in airgap installs.
- [ ] Decide on naming — local-devkit vs redwood-playground-cli

Notes to self / fragments
- Could include a "seed prompts" gallery for common product patterns (summarization, Q&A, chat).
- Think about a "record-and-replay" feature to capture request/response pairs to reproduce flakiness. Might be 2.0.
- If customers ask, provide an audited minimal runtime container for on-prem PoCs.

Next steps (this sprint)
- Quick spike: 2d to implement the mock backend + start command. Demo to DX and Solutions on Wed.
- Gather packaging recommendation from infra (ask @sam-ortiz).

Slack refs / bookmarks
- #dx-local-devkit (placeholder)
- PR proto branch: github.com/redwood-inference/local-devkit-proto

End of brainstorm (rough).
summary: Brainstorm for a minimal local developer runtime/CLI (local-devkit). Goals, personas, MVP, CLI UX, security notes, open questions and a TODO list.
